title: Angels from the Realms of Glory
description: James Montgomery's Christmas hymn to Henry Smart's tune Regent Square, in Smart's four parts as Charles L. Hutchins printed them in 1894, for 2 to 4 singers: verses 1 to 3, the angels, the shepherds and the sages, each ending in the refrain "Come and worship". The tune climbs to its highest note on "Worship Christ" and comes home on "the new-born King".

credits.arrangement: Henry Smart's four parts (as printed by Charles L. Hutchins, 1894), adapted by Stackapella

licence.arrangement: Smart's four parts as printed in Hutchins's Church Hymnal (headed "Regent Square", "H. Smart"; Smart died 1879; the book's editor Charles L. Hutchins died 1920; public domain), the same chords as Smart's first printing of the tune (1866) and the 1871 page below where compared: his tune unchanged in its metre, a tone lower, and his chords, with these changes for 2 to 4 beginners (pitches as written here, in B-flat): every lower part sings one note a syllable where Smart moves within one (5 places: the alto and bass under "cre-", the tenor under "Mes-", the tenor and bass under "Christ", the alto under "the" and "born"); on "glo-ry," the alto sings D4 (Smart holds F4 under the tune: a bare fourth, then a unison); on "Wing" the tenor holds B-flat 3 (his G3, doubling the tune's G, the E-flat chord's third); on "flight o'er" the alto sings D4 and the tenor B-flat 3 (his B-flat 3 and F3, then B-flat 3 and G3), so the duet has thirds and sixths, and on "all" the tenor C4 (his F3, which would move in octaves with the tune); on "sang" the alto sings D4 and the tenor B-flat 3 (his F4 and F3); on "cre-" the alto sings his first note, F4, the bass his second, C3, and the tenor A3 (his F3), so the passing F chord on C has its third (his alto's E-flat 4 after the F4 would be a second under the tune, rising to F4); on "a-" the alto sings F4 (his D4, an octave under the tune) and holds it on "tion's" (his E-flat 4, a seventh that would rise to the alto's G4 on "sto-"), so the two quick dominant chords under "cre-" and "tion's" are sung without their seventh; on "sto-ry, Now pro-" the alto sings G4, F-sharp 4, G4, F-sharp 4 (his D4 throughout) and the tenor B-flat 3 on "sto-" (his G3) and D4 on "ry, Now pro-" (his F-sharp 3, G3, F-sharp 3), so the D chord has its third at every size; on "Mes-" the tenor sings B-flat 3; on "Come and" (the refrain's first two notes) the alto sings A4 and the tenor C4 (his F4 and A3), a third under the tune; on the second "and wor-" the alto sings A-flat 4 then G4 and the tenor D4 then E-flat 4 (his D4 and A-flat 3, exchanged, then E-flat 4 and G3), so the duet sings thirds, the seventh falls and the leading tone rises into the E-flat chord; on "new-" the alto sings D4 and the tenor B-flat 3 (his F4 and C4, the tune's B-flat suspended over an F chord), a B-flat chord over the bass's F, and on "born" the alto E-flat 4 on the beat; the verses 2 and 3 sung to the same parts; breaths written in for beginners at Smart's couplets (the held "earth" and "birth" give up a beat), with a bar's rest between verses. Accepted exceptions: the alto's moves are 57% steps and repeats, under the beginner rule's 70%, as its thirds under the tune cost leaps of a third or fourth (Smart's own alto, which holds one note under the tune, passes but leaves bare fifths and unisons at "story", "Now proclaim" and "Come and worship"); Smart's alto leaps a fifth to "from" and falls a third (an alto D4 there would move in octaves with the bass); Smart's bass keeps its leaps of a fifth (two in the first line and in the refrain), its octave up into the second line, and its octave down on "born" into the last cadence; the duet keeps Smart's bare fourths on "from", "all" (a third would double the leading tone with the bass) and "claim" (it would cross under the tenor), and his unisons on "cre-", on "birth", where his alto's E rises to the tune's F as a two-part close (a third there left the four-part leading tone and seventh unresolved), and on "ship," before the second "Come"; the alto's F-sharp under "pro-" falls to D on "claim", where the tune takes the G; the trio has no third on the quick chords under "of", "cre-", "tion's" and the second "and" (the tenor has it in four parts), under "Mes-" until the tune's second note, and on "birth" and "ship,", and no root under "realms" (Smart's own chord, a D minor sound on F), "ry," and "flight" (the tenor holds it in four parts).
licence.source: Charles L. Hutchins, ed., The Church Hymnal, revised and enlarged in accordance with the action of the General Convention of the Protestant Episcopal Church ... 1892 (Boston: The Parish Choir, 1894; organ edition, preface dated Advent 1894), No. 60, p. 82, "Regent Square", "H. Smart", "J. Montgomery", 8.7.8.7.4.7, crotchet = 100, in four parts in C, 4/4, written here a tone lower in B-flat; verse 1 as printed under the music and verses 2 and 3 as printed below it ("Shepherds in the field abiding", "Sages, leave your contemplations"), whose refrain lines "Come and worship, / Worship Christ, the new-born King" are sung as verse 1 prints them under the notes, "Come and worship" twice; his verse 4, "Saints before the altar bending", is left out; Princeton Theological Seminary Library copy, read from the scan at archive.org/details/chuevi00hutc/page/n133 (its tune index, p. xxix, n32: "Regent Square ... Henry Smart, 1867"). Compared with Smart's first printing of the tune, Psalms and Hymns for Divine Worship (London: James Nisbet and Co., 1866), p. 58, "Regent Square", in C in 4/2, to other words (Nos. 126 and 127, "Bright with all his crowns of glory" and "Glory be to God the Father"), whose refrain lines carry the same four parts (archive.org/details/fordi00pres/page/n273); and with the earliest printing of these words with this tune seen, The Baptist Praise Book (New York: A. S. Barnes and Co., 1871), p. 108, "Regent Square", "Sir H. Smart", hymn 271 printed below hymn 270, in C in 4/2, the same four parts in its last line (archive.org/details/baptistpraiseboo71full/page/n117); the words checked against Montgomery's The Christian Psalmist (Glasgow, 1825), No. 487, "Good tidings of great joy to all people", pp. 389 and 390 (archive.org/details/christianpsalmis00montiala/page/n406), where the refrain is "Come and worship, / Worship Christ the new-born King." once
